nota: Curated naval deployments for docs/data/mobili.json, read by raccogli.py. Every item cites at least one open source (key in 'fonti_rif'). Positions are area-level estimates: lat/lon is the centre of the area named by the source (or the port), precisione_km is the radius of that area, 'sim' (optional) is only where the symbol is drawn inside the circle. Text in English. Update 'data_evento' only when a newer dated source is added. Last full review: 2026-11-10.

elementi.note: Japan's main ship for Quad exercise Malabar 2026 (US, Japan, Australia, India), held south of Kanto from 5 to 12 November per the JMSDF. On 5-6 November the participating ships were docked in Yokosuka for the shore phase (USNI). Circle covers the port and the announced exercise area; no ship position given.

Escorting Russian cargo convoys out of the Baltic: through the Danish straits on 1 November with ANASTASIIA, ASCALON and tanker Elnya, back east through the Fehmarn Belt on 3 November, through the Great Belt on 7 November with LADY D. On 8 November a Sentinel-1 radar image showed MAIA-1, LADY R, LADY D and a vessel without AIS, likely Stoykiy, in the Kattegat, watched by HDMS Rota. OSINT, no official confirmation.
Monitoring the Russian convoy escorted by corvette Stoykiy in the Kattegat on 8 November (Sentinel-1 image identified by OSINT analysts).
Shadowed by HMS Dauntless and HMS Tyne from 1 to 14 October while escorting sanctioned cargo ships through the English Channel (Royal Navy, 2 Nov). Pennant number as printed by USNI.

Shadowed Russian frigate Neustrashimy (1-14 Oct) and landing ship Aleksandr Shabalin (11-14 Oct) in the Channel.

elementi.dettaglio: Russian Black Sea Fleet main base
elementi.note: Ukraine's Navy said on 26 October that the Black Sea Fleet had not left port for five months and fires Kalibr missiles from Novorossiysk. Ukrainian claim, not independently confirmed. Satellite images in August showed at least four ships damaged there by Ukrainian strikes (Naval News). Turkiye keeps the straits closed to warships of the belligerents, so these ships cannot reach the Mediterranean.

elementi.dettaglio: Santa Maria-class frigate, EUNAVFOR Atalanta flagship
elementi.note: Flagship of EU Operation Atalanta (Task Force 465) since 10 October, with Portuguese Commodore Jose Rodrigues Pedra commanding the 54th rotation. Moored in Djibouti on 3 November for a visit by the EU Political and Security Committee; embarks an SH-60B and a ScanEagle drone. Atalanta has handled seven piracy cases off Somalia and Yemen since April 2026.

Named by USNI on 28 September as flagship of EU Operation Aspides, which escorts merchant ships against Houthi attacks. On 12 October Euronews wrote that Italy and Greece supply the mission's three core ships and that only the Netherlands and Belgium had offered one more ship each; EU High Representative Kallas said at least ten are needed. No newer dated position found.

elementi.regione: Bab el-Mandeb and southern Red Sea
elementi.note: One of two French frigates deployed near Bab el-Mandeb. In the night of 1-2 October it shot down with its gun a drone approaching the CMA CGM container ship Champs-Elysees in the strait (Le Monde, confirmed by the French Joint Staff). The French Joint Staff said in mid-October that its Aspides frigate escorts about two ships a day.

Sent from the Baltic to be ready for mine clearance in the Strait of Hormuz, which has not started. In mid-October, while transiting Bab el-Mandeb under French escort, a French warship intercepted a ballistic missile, probably Houthi, near it (De Morgen, 26 Oct, via Naval News). Date approximate.

elementi.dettaglio: Bay-class landing ship, mine countermeasures mothership
elementi.regione: Western Indian Ocean (AIS north of Zanzibar in late September)
elementi.note: After HMS Dragon returned to Portsmouth on 9 October, the only Royal Navy ship near the Strait of Hormuz, waiting for the multinational mine-clearance mission (USNI, 12 Oct). AIS placed it north of Zanzibar in late September.

elementi.regione: Gulf of Aden and waters off Somalia (mission area)
elementi.note: Japan's counter-piracy destroyer in the Gulf of Aden as of 2 October (Joint Staff), also gathering information for safe navigation in the Middle East; to be relieved by JS Kirisame. On 6 November Japan extended both missions to 19 November 2027. Mission area only.

elementi.regione: South China Sea, Philippine EEZ (last report, en route to the Gulf of Aden)
elementi.note: Due to leave Sasebo on 17 October as Japan's 55th counter-piracy surface force for the Gulf of Aden. On 23 October it drilled with Philippine and US Coast Guard ships in the Philippine EEZ in the South China Sea. Last reported position; now probably further west.
